newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspended terms asked in Socialist corruption case.
newsitem.headline: Suspended terms asked in Socialist corruption case.

text.p: A public prosecutor on Thursday requested suspended prison terms for two former treasurers of France's opposition Socialists for running an illicit party fundraising scheme.
The prosecutor asked that Henri Emmanuelli, one of the party's national leaders, and Andre Laignel, be banned from standing for office for an unspecified period.

Prosecutor Philippe Cretin also called for 18-month suspended sentences against two former Socialist parliamentarians, Michel Pezet and Philippe Sanmarco, as well as a ban on their standing for election for two years.

Emmanuelli and Laignel said at the trial earlier this week they took political responsibility for schemes to funnel funds to the party via a consultancy firm in the late 1980s but they maintained they had not broken any laws.
"I fully accept the existence of these consultancy companies. They took part in financing the Socialist Party," Emmanuelli, who was treasurer from 1988 until 1991, told the court on Monday.
Laignel, treasurer from 1981-88, used the same defence as Emmanuelli, saying that laws had since been tightened.
Emmanuelli, who was briefly leader of the Socialist party in 1994-95, has already been convicted on similar charges in an earlier trial in Brittany in 1995.
He was given a one-year suspended sentence and 30,000 franc ($6,000) fine for receiving illicit campaign contributions from the front company known as Urba, run by party insiders.
Emmanuelli is now on trial for handling stolen goods and for influence peddling and Laignel is on trial for complicity in the same charges.
In the earlier trial, investigators uncovered a covert funding network used by the Socialists to finance their campaigns by taking rake-offs from public works contracts via front companies like Urba.
The front companies allegedly demanded consulting fees from companies seeking public tenders, and part of that money was then funnelled to local Socialist candidates and the national party.

The current trial, which began on March 3 and is expected to last a month, is based on similar accusations, again involving the Urba consultancy firm, but this time involving party operations in the Mediterranean port city of Marseilles.
Prosecutors say the party illegally raked off 9.4 million francs ($1.65 million) from public works contracts awarded in the region during 1988 and 1989.
